comment: The world: where each region stands on a grid of chunks (the unit a simulation owns), and the sea between them. A region is its recipe, content/regions/<id>.json, and what it places, in the folder beside it (content/regions/<id>/): written in world coordinates, its grid covering exactly its chunks: its terrain's origin at their middle, its cells times its cell their size. Emberholm, the first region, is 6 x 6 chunks round the world's origin. Wherever no region stands is open sea, `sea.depth` metres deep; the edge of the world is the edge of every region's chunks together. Where two regions meet, or a region meets the open sea, the ground either side of the border is blended over `blend` metres so it meets with no seam: every region's cell is the same size, a whole number of them to a chunk.
